messages:
customer_integration: Hey team — we started getting 429s for org=org-acme-ux during the nightly ingest at 2026-02-12T03:12Z. Attached one raw response header: `X-RateLimit-Limit: 600\nX-RateLimit-Remaining: 0\nX-RateLimit-Reset: 2026-02-12T03:13:00Z` Client says they send short bursts ~12 reqs/sec for ~10s every minute from ~50 workers. Any quick triage tips?

alex_w: Thanks — can you paste the full response headers (including `Retry-After` / `X-Request-Id`) and the org id numeric? Also what endpoint (chat/generate/embeddings)?

customer_integration: Endpoint is `/v1/chat/completions` (chat). Full headers from one response: `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nRetry-After: 10\nX-RateLimit-Limit: 600\nX-RateLimit-Remaining: 0\nX-RateLimit-Reset: 2026-02-12T03:13:00Z\nX-Request-Id: r-9f3a2b`

maria_l: Chat = token-heavy. Important: RPM = requests/min, TPM = tokens/min. Are they counting tokens per message? Long context spikes token TPM quickly. Do they stream?

customer_integration: They send non-streaming, messages are short (~50 tokens each). So each request ~50 tokens.

sanjay_r: Looking at gateway logs around `2026-02-12T03:12Z` I see repeated entries: `throttle=hit org=org-acme-ux reqs_60s=1180 rpm_limit=600 tokens_60s=62000 tpm_limit=60000` — looks like rolling 60s window exceeded both RPM and TPM briefly. The gateway uses sliding window sampling, not simple fixed-minute buckets.

opsbot: ALERT: 429-surge-detected org-acme-ux at 2026-02-12T03:12:18Z. Incident INC-10235 created.

elaine: Immediate user-facing advice: honor `Retry-After` header (backoff 10s), add jitter, and smooth request bursts across the minute. Suggested client-side change: limit concurrency to 10 workers and use exponential backoff with full jitter. Example (psuedo):
```
sleep = min(60, base * 2**attempt) + random() * jitter
```
Also prefer streaming (if available) to keep long-lived connection and reduce per-request overhead.

alex_w: For reproduction, ask customer to run this curl once during a quiet window and paste logs: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Request-Id: test-123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -d @sample.json` Include `X-RateLimit-*` response headers.

customer_integration: Repro run attached — got `Retry-After: 9`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, trace id `r-9f3a2b`. They also confirmed they kick off 50 worker processes at the top of every minute (cron alignment).

maria_l: Cron alignment is the culprit — synchronized spikes look like a thundering herd. Recommend staggering jobs across minute window (eg random delay 0-60s) or shard by second offsets. Also consider token budgeting: reduce prompt length if possible.

sanjay_r: On our side we can consider short-term mitigation: bump the org's soft RPM to 1200 for 24h while they roll out staggered cron. Need approval from quota team. I see quota config: `rpm:600 tpm:60000`.

alex_w: Please open a support ticket with customer consent for a temporary quota bump and include the `r-9f3a2b` trace and sample logs. I'll paste suggested text for the quota team.

customer_integration: Created case SUP-4472 with logs and consent. Thanks — will implement staggering today.

sam_t: I'll pick this up with Quota. Tagging @quota-team. Proposal: temporary RPM increase to 1200 and TPM to 110000 for 48 hours, monitor metrics. If they still exceed, we revert.

elaine: Also add client guidance doc link: https://console.redwood.ai/docs/rate-limits — includes best practices and backoff code.

alex_w: Follow-ups: 1) confirm client deploys staggering 2) confirm support ticket INC-10235 / SUP-4472 linked 3) monitor X-RateLimit-Remaining and our alerts for next 6 hours.

customer_integration: Stagger deployed, initial 10 minutes look good — no 429s so far. Will report back if any regressions. Thanks all :thumbsup:
